query: How has Marcus's engagement with traffic and safety issues on Maple Street changed over the sessions?
gold: Marcus mentioned traffic concerns incidentally in Session 1 (worried about scaffolding blocking the school gate during works) but did not escalate. By Session 3, after a car reversed toward his son at the school gate without seeing him, Marcus shifted immediately to formal escalation: 'As a parent this has to be dealt with. I'm raising this formally today.' From that point his engagement intensified — he frames almost every subsequent safety or development discussion through the lens of child safety at the school gate, and he follows up unresolved threads rather than letting them drop.
context:

[2] (about=Marcus, episodic, t2 @2025-05-12T15:35:00) I'm in favour. As a parent, the school gate situation is untenable, people park on the pavement all morning. Permits would fix that overnight.

[11] (about=Marcus, core, t3 @2025-05-19T08:47:00) will formally raise the near-miss incident at the school gate with a car reversing off no. 19's driveway, where his son was nearly hit

agent_answer:
Earlier (t2, 12 May), Marcus was in favour of parking permits, citing the school gate as "untenable" with people parking on the pavement all morning — a general parental concern about traffic/safety.

After the near-miss on 19 May, where a car reversing off no. 19's driveway nearly hit his son, his engagement became personal, urgent and formal: he said he was "raising this formally today," and he remained "still properly shaken" while thanking the group for support. So his engagement shifted from supporting a general mitigation (permits) to taking direct, formal action on a specific incident, driven by the near-miss to his own child.
